objective_for_doctor: Evaluate a 67-year-old woman with a change in mental status and abdominal discomfort.

turns.doctor_opening: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on?
turns.patient_opening: Doctor: Hello—what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what’s been going on? Patient: I’ve been feeling very confused lately and I can’t seem to explain what I’m feeling very well. I also had a fever around 102°F and I feel discomfort when the right upper part of my belly is touched.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any change in the shape or contour of either breast—such as one breast looking different from before, a new dimpling, or a change in how it sits? (Yes or no)
turns.patient_answer: “No—I haven’t noticed any changes in my breasts, and neither one looks different from before.”

turns.doctor_question: I’m sorry you’re dealing with this. Have you been experiencing any abdominal (belly) pain recently?
turns.patient_answer: Patient: Yes, I’ve had discomfort in the right upper part of my belly, especially when it’s touched. I don’t always have clear, persistent pain I can describe, but it does feel tender there.

turns.doctor_question: Are you feeling generally weak all over—more than usual—rather than just tired from one specific activity?
turns.patient_answer: Patient: Yes, I feel more weak all over than usual, and it’s worse than simple tiredness.

turns.doctor_question: Have you had diarrhea recently (loose or watery stools)?
turns.patient_answer: Patient: I haven’t had diarrhea or loose, watery stools recently.

turns.doctor_question: Are you having **profuse sweating**—like sweating a lot even when you’re not doing anything strenuous or when the room isn’t hot?
turns.patient_answer: I don’t think I’ve had sweating like that—nothing unusually heavy even when I’m just resting. I’ve mostly been dealing with the confusion, the fever, and the tenderness in the right upper belly area.

turns.doctor_question: Do you currently have pain in your wrist? (yes or no)
turns.patient_answer: Patient: No, I don’t have pain in my wrist. I’ve mostly been dealing with confusion, a fever around 102°F, and tenderness when my right upper belly is touched.

turns.doctor_question: Do you usually have morning stiffness that lasts **more than 30 minutes** after you wake up? (Yes or no)
turns.patient_answer: Patient: No, I don’t have morning stiffness lasting more than 30 minutes. I’ve mainly been dealing with confusion, a fever around 102°F, and discomfort when my right upper abdomen is touched.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed a breast lump or mass that feels **fixed in place**—meaning it doesn’t move much when you gently press it? (Yes or no)
turns.patient_answer: “No— I haven’t noticed any breast lump or fixed mass; I haven’t felt anything like that when gently pressing.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you currently have any pain in your knee (yes or no)?
turns.patient_answer: Patient: No, I don’t have any pain in my knee. My main issues have been the confusion, the fever around 102°F, and the discomfort when the right upper part of my belly is touched.

turns.doctor_question: When you walk, do you get pain or cramping in your calf that improves or goes away when you stop and rest? (yes/no)
turns.patient_answer: Patient: No, I haven’t noticed any calf pain or cramping when I walk. My main concerns have been the confusion, the fever around 102°F, and the tenderness in the right upper part of my belly.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed a **firm, hard lump or mass in your thigh** that feels different from the surrounding tissue? (Yes/No)
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any firm hard lump or unusual mass in my thigh.”

turns.doctor_question: I’m sorry you’re dealing with this. **Have you noticed any vision loss that happened without pain** (for example, blurry vision or loss of vision that isn’t accompanied by eye pain)?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any vision loss or blurry vision that started without pain—I’ve mainly been dealing with confusion and the fever, along with tenderness in my right upper belly when it’s touched.”
